title: Operating and diagnosing PostgreSQL
brief: Use PostgreSQL evidence to separate blocked work, excessive work and connection pressure.
outcomes: Trace a request through pool and server waits
Test a targeted operational intervention and its recovery cost
entry: General incident triage and a PostgreSQL application connection; prepare native plans or vacuum only for the selected investigation.

neighbours.RL113: Supplies native plan interpretation before an execution/spill repair.
neighbours.RL111: Supplies vacuum and retained-horizon understanding before maintenance changes.
neighbours.RL91: Supplies any missing lock/wait reasoning before a blocker intervention.

heading.title: Where time is spent
heading.brief: Start from RL103’s selected symptom; introduce the session, wait and query identifiers needed to correlate request/pool timing with pg_stat_activity, waits and query statistics. Explain sampling, reset and visibility limits; a blocked-request investigation need not first learn native plan repair or vacuum.

heading.title: A blocked purchase
heading.brief: For a blocker branch, fill any missing lock reasoning from RL91, then inspect blockers, transaction age and locks in an owned reproduction; separate cancellation from termination and account for rollback.

heading.title: Spills and pressure
heading.brief: For an execution or maintenance branch, prepare native plan interpretation in RL113 or retained-horizon reasoning in RL111 as needed. Relate the observed work to buffers, temporary I/O, per-operator memory and active sessions; avoid multiplying work_mem as a simple server-wide budget.

heading.title: An intervention and follow-up
heading.brief: Measure targeted admission, query or maintenance changes; verify errors, latency, queue drain and storage headroom after the symptom falls.
